questions.question_en: Consider a system that uses 5 bits for representing signed integers in 2's complement format. Two integers A and B are represented as A = 01010 and B = 11010. Which one of the following operations will result in an arithmetic overflow?
questions.question_hi:
[Digital Logic (2's Complement Overflow) • GATE CSE (CS) • Feb 2024]
Consider a system that uses 5 bits for representing signed integers in 2's complement format. Two integers A and B are represented as A = 01010 and B = 11010. Which one of the following operations will result in an arithmetic overflow?
options_en: A − B
A + B
B − A
A & B
options_hi: A − B
A + B
B − A
A & B
questions.explanation_en: In 5-bit 2's complement (representable range −16 to +15), A = 01010₂ = +10 and B = 11010₂ = −16 + 8 + 2 = −6. Computing A − B = 10 − (−6) = +16 exceeds the maximum positive value +15, resulting in a signed arithmetic overflow.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (GATE CSE (CS) • Feb 2024):
In 5-bit 2's complement (representable range −16 to +15), A = 01010₂ = +10 and B = 11010₂ = −16 + 8 + 2 = −6. Computing A − B = 10 − (−6) = +16 exceeds the maximum positive value +15, resulting in a signed arithmetic overflow.

questions.question_en: Let f : R → R be defined as f(x) = max{x, x³}. The set of all points in R where f(x) is NOT differentiable is:
questions.question_hi:
[Engineering Mathematics (Piecewise Differentiability) • GATE CSE (CS) • Feb 2024]
Let f : R → R be defined as f(x) = max{x, x³}. The set of all points in R where f(x) is NOT differentiable is:
questions.explanation_en: The curves y = x and y = x³ intersect where x³ − x = x(x − 1)(x + 1) = 0, i.e., at x = −1, 0, 1. At each of these three points the left and right derivatives of max{x, x³} differ (1 vs 3 at x = ±1; 0 vs 1 at x = 0), so f is non-differentiable at {−1, 0, 1}.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (GATE CSE (CS) • Feb 2024):
The curves y = x and y = x³ intersect where x³ − x = x(x − 1)(x + 1) = 0, i.e., at x = −1, 0, 1. At each of these three points the left and right derivatives of max{x, x³} differ (1 vs 3 at x = ±1; 0 vs 1 at x = 0), so f is non-differentiable at {−1, 0, 1}.

questions.question_en: A 32-bit processor has a 64 KB, 4-way set-associative cache with a cache block (line) size of 64 bytes. The number of bits in the Tag, Set Index, and Byte Offset fields of the physical address are, respectively:
questions.question_hi:
[Computer Organization (Cache Memory Mapping) • GATE CSE (CS) • Feb 2024]
A 32-bit processor has a 64 KB, 4-way set-associative cache with a cache block (line) size of 64 bytes. The number of bits in the Tag, Set Index, and Byte Offset fields of the physical address are, respectively:
questions.explanation_en: Block size = 64 B = 2⁶ B => Byte Offset = 6 bits. Total cache lines = 64 KB / 64 B = 1024 lines. With 4-way set associativity, Number of sets = 1024 / 4 = 256 = 2⁸ sets => Set Index = 8 bits. Tag bits = 32 − (8 + 6) = 18 bits.

Which of the following statement(s) about database concurrency control is/are TRUE?

Strict Two-Phase Locking (Strict 2PL) guarantees both conflict serializability and cascadeless recoverability.

options_hi: A schedule S is conflict-serializable if and only if its precedence (serialization) graph is acyclic.

A sender uses the Selective Repeat sliding window protocol over a 10 Mbps link with a one-way propagation delay of 20 ms and a frame size of 10,000 bits. To achieve 100% link utilization (ignoring ACKs and header overhead), the minimum required sender window size W (in frames) is ________.
questions.explanation_en: Transmission time T_t = L / B = 10,000 bits / (10 × 10⁶ bps) = 1 ms. Round-trip propagation delay 2 T_p = 2 × 20 ms = 40 ms. For 100% utilization, W / (1 + 2a) ≥ 1 => W = 1 + 2(T_p / T_t) = 1 + 40/1 = 41 frames.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (GATE CSE (CS) • Feb 2024):
Transmission time T_t = L / B = 10,000 bits / (10 × 10⁶ bps) = 1 ms. Round-trip propagation delay 2 T_p = 2 × 20 ms = 40 ms. For 100% utilization, W / (1 + 2a) ≥ 1 => W = 1 + 2(T_p / T_t) = 1 + 40/1 = 41 frames.

questions.question_en: A paged virtual memory system uses a Translation Lookaside Buffer (TLB) with a hit ratio of 90%. A TLB lookup takes 10 ns and a main memory access takes 100 ns (assuming TLB lookup and memory access are sequential, and a single-level page table in main memory). The Effective Memory Access Time (EMAT) in nanoseconds (assuming 0 page faults) is ________.
questions.question_hi:
[Operating Systems (Effective Memory Access Time) • GATE CSE (CS) • Feb 2024]
A paged virtual memory system uses a Translation Lookaside Buffer (TLB) with a hit ratio of 90%. A TLB lookup takes 10 ns and a main memory access takes 100 ns (assuming TLB lookup and memory access are sequential, and a single-level page table in main memory). The Effective Memory Access Time (EMAT) in nanoseconds (assuming 0 page faults) is ________.
questions.explanation_en: On a TLB hit (90%): time = TLB (10 ns) + 1 memory access (100 ns) = 110 ns. On a TLB miss (10%): time = TLB (10 ns) + page table access (100 ns) + data access (100 ns) = 210 ns. EMAT = 0.90 × 110 + 0.10 × 210 = 99 + 21 = 120 ns.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (GATE CSE (CS) • Feb 2024):
On a TLB hit (90%): time = TLB (10 ns) + 1 memory access (100 ns) = 110 ns. On a TLB miss (10%): time = TLB (10 ns) + page table access (100 ns) + data access (100 ns) = 210 ns. EMAT = 0.90 × 110 + 0.10 × 210 = 99 + 21 = 120 ns.

questions.question_en: Over the alphabet Σ = {0, 1}, the minimum number of states in a Deterministic Finite Automaton (DFA) that accepts all binary strings whose decimal value is divisible by 5 (with the empty string ε rejected or treated as 0 — wait: if 0 is accepted from start state, how many remainder states mod 5 exist?) is ________.

questions.explanation_en: By the Myhill-Nerode Theorem, two binary strings x and y are distinguishable iff x ≢ y (mod 5). Since there are 5 residue classes modulo 5 ({0, 1, 2, 3, 4}), the minimal DFA has exactly 5 states.

questions.question_en: A B+ tree internal node has block size 1024 bytes, search key size 12 bytes, and block pointer size 8 bytes. The maximum number of block pointers (order p) that can fit in one internal node is ________.
questions.question_hi:
[DBMS (B+ Tree Order & Fanout) • GATE CSE (CS) • Feb 2024]
A B+ tree internal node has block size 1024 bytes, search key size 12 bytes, and block pointer size 8 bytes. The maximum number of block pointers (order p) that can fit in one internal node is ________.
questions.explanation_en: An internal node of order p contains p block pointers and (p − 1) search keys: 8p + 12(p − 1) ≤ 1024 => 20p − 12 ≤ 1024 => 20p ≤ 1036 => p = ⌊1036 / 20⌋ = 51.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (GATE CSE (CS) • Feb 2024):
An internal node of order p contains p block pointers and (p − 1) search keys: 8p + 12(p − 1) ≤ 1024 => 20p − 12 ≤ 1024 => 20p ≤ 1036 => p = ⌊1036 / 20⌋ = 51.
